_comment: Synthetic DORA Art. 18 RTS inputs, per scenario -- build-spec §6.5: 'say so in the docstring rather than pretending the numbers are real.' These are lab fixtures for the platform's example tenant, Meridian Pay (docs/00-scope.md §0.1.2: ~2,400 SME merchants, ~40M transactions/year, 11-country EU passporting), not measurements of a real incident. See classify.py for how these combine with the drill record's own real, measured fields (duration, data loss).

ns-restore._comment: Namespace-level delete+restore: a contained incident by design (one tenant workload, one region) -- these numbers are chosen to be plausible for that shape of fault, not tuned to force a particular classification outcome.

node-kill._comment: A single worker node going unreachable: same contained, single-tenant shape as ns-restore -- one node, one workload, no cross-border spread.

pvc-corruption-restore._comment: Silent data corruption caught by the hash chain: same contained, single-tenant shape -- the numbers stay identical to ns-restore/node-kill since none of the three scenarios differ in real business-impact scope, only in fault mechanism.

network-partition._comment: A deliberate, bounded, self-healed Cilium deny -- no client-facing impact at all (this drill validates enforcement, it doesn't simulate a real outage), so every synthetic input stays at its floor rather than being padded to force a classification outcome.
